'''Richard W. Kenyon''' (born 1964) is an American mathematician known for his contributions in [[combinatorics]] and [[probability theory]]. He is the Erastus L. DeForest Professor of Mathematics at [[Yale University]].

Kenyon graduated from [[Rice University]] and then earned his PhD under supervision of [[William Thurston]] at [[Princeton University]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Richard W. Kenyon's CV |work=Brown University |url=https://www.math.brown.edu/~rkenyon/ccv.pdf |access-date=March 29, 2016 |archive-date=July 9, 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130709093001/http://www.math.brown.edu/~rkenyon/ccv.pdf |url-status=dead }}</ref> He won the [[Rollo Davidson Prize]] in 2001 and the [[Loève Prize]] in 2007. In 2014 Kenyon was chosen as a [[Simons Investigator]] and inducted into the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]. In 2018, he was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers#2018, Rio de Janeiro|invited speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in Rio de Janeiro.
